parsed.explanation: No express trans-specific offence, documented trans detention, facility ban, or official violence is recorded, but de facto prosecution of public same-sex conduct under vague morality provisions, no SOGI anti-discrimination remedy, banned LGBTI organisations, and pervasive social/religious intolerance create a hostile combined regime. Thin documentation and unbounded case law mean silence is not safety; structural signals extrapolate toward risk if outed, without reaching routine trans-specific state targeting seen at 0.35.

entry_documents.exposure: Foreign marker treatment not documented; no domestic recognition framework exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Whether an amended foreign passport affects entry or processing remains uncertain and unanswered.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Sections 353/354 retain power to prosecute public same-sex conduct, treated de facto illegal; trans-specific detention not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visible presentation read as same-sex conduct in public could trigger the vague morality provisions; scope is unbounded by case law.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No general remedy for refusal of service or facility entry on SOGI grounds; no specific facility-access law documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility refusal has no legal prohibition to invoke, leaving only a complaint route.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Status and conduct taboo, pervasive social and religious intolerance, no public discussion tolerated, LGBTI organisations cannot register.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Climate of intolerance plus morality-law leverage increases risk if trans identity is read as same-sex conduct.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Societal pattern of discrimination and fear of family/community shunning documented; no official violence cases cited in 2023.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Complaints can be filed with police or national human-rights commission.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse exists as a channel but no anti-discrimination law defines the wrong; effectiveness not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No SOGI discrimination prohibition outside employment; no case law bounds Sections 353/354; documentation is thin and largely non-trans-specific.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Police and national human-rights commission complaint route documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin recourse plus unresolved legal scope means outcomes if outed cannot be reliably bounded from the dossier.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-B: that anchor documents routine police stops, confiscations and fines specifically for trans visitors; here no trans-specific police targeting, detention or fines are documented.

Lower than 0.55-B: that anchor has administrative screening with written decisions and appeals and no pervasive intolerance; here de facto morality prosecution, no SOGI remedy and pervasive intolerance dominate.
Lower than 0.65-A: that anchor has explicit equality protection, reliable court release, apology and compensation after a brief hold; none of those operative protections are documented here.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: vague morality provisions provide a state lever if presentation is read as public same-sex conduct, while pervasive intolerance and absence of anti-discrimination law remove legal recourse beyond police/NHRC complaints. No universal trans-specific border, facility or custody regime is documented, and 2023 reporting cites no official violence, keeping the case above routine-targeting anchors. Thin, non-incident documentation, banned organisations and unbounded statutory scope nevertheless extrapolate risk upward if outed, for solo adults and visibly travelling families alike, with no documented minor-specific rule.
